problem: Zero-shot (M)LLM VLN agents rely only on local observations (~3 m), lacking the global spatial priors learning-based agents acquire from large-scale training. This yields short-sighted decisions, inefficient exploration and ambiguity when several instruction-consistent options exist, leaving a large gap to supervised agents.
motivation: Household robots (e.g. vacuum cleaners) operate in bounded environments and rarely switch scenes, so pre-exploring is realistic. Pre-exploration gives a 3D reconstruction that could supply global layout and semantics to a zero-shot agent, compensating for missing learned spatial priors.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical Spatial Scene Graph (floor-room-object) from a pre-explored point cloud and query it at each step to give a zero-shot MLLM agent an agent-centric top-down map, a compass-aligned panorama, and remote object semantics around candidate locations.
insight: Explicit global spatial information is a strong, agent-agnostic signal: adding the spatial map to NavGPT raises SR from 43.5 to 52.1 on R2R-sampled, and adding it to SmartWay raises R2R-CE SR from 51.0 to 62.0. Remote object semantics only help when paired with visual panoramas: under text-only observations they hurt (SR 66→60 with GT annotations) because of ambiguity between current and future objects, whereas compass visual input gives SR 72. Ground-truth annotations beat predicted ones, so annotation quality matters. A spatial-map-only agent with no visual input already reaches 40.8 SR.
method: Spatial Scene Graph construction: 4-stage pipeline on the point cloud: floor segmentation (height histogram + DBSCAN), room segmentation (geometric heuristic of Bobkov et al., manual check of regions >20 m²), room classification (GPT-5 on frames from each room), object detection (SpatialLM fine-tuned on Matterport3D training scans). Result is a floor-room-object containment hierarchy.
Agent-centric spatial map: localizes the agent's floor via Z and room via XY, then projects rooms within ~7.68 m (1024x1024 map, 0.015 m/grid) onto a top-down map with heading always up.
Compass-like visual observation: 8 views at 45° steps (FOV 90°, 256x256) tiled in a 3x3 grid around a central compass, giving a 1024x1024 image (~640 tokens versus >1700 for sequential images).

Remote object localization: for each candidate navigable place (nav-graph nodes, or waypoint-predictor outputs from SmartWay in continuous environments), retrieves objects in the same room, grouped by category with distances, as text.

MLLM decision maker: GPT-5.1 receives map, compass image, remote object text, history and instruction and predicts the next action. The variant SpatialNav† uses ground-truth Matterport3D annotations as an upper bound.

setting.backbone: GPT-5.1 (frozen); Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen3-VL-Plus in ablations; SpatialLM fine-tuned for object detection and GPT-5 for room classification in SSG construction
setting.training_data: none (training-free agent); only SpatialLM detector fine-tuned on Matterport3D training scans for SSG construction
setting.observation: 8-view panoramic RGB (compass image) plus SSG-derived top-down map, agent pose, and object semantics from a pre-explored 3D point cloud
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (R2R, REVERIE); predicted waypoints with low-level control in Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE)
setting.privileged: Pre-exploration: full 3D point cloud of the environment (Matterport3D reconstruction), agent pose/coordinates, manually corrected room segmentation for large regions; SpatialNav† additionally uses GT room/object annotations.

numbers_note: Some SR/SPL values are printed at integer precision for baselines. Ablation tables use other sampled subsets (R2R 267 trajectories, REVERIE 230 trajectories over 56 scans; 50 trajectories over 5 scans), which are not listed here.
results: SpatialNav reaches SR 57.7 (R2R), 49.6 (REVERIE), 64.0 (R2R-CE) and 32.4 (RxR-CE) on val-unseen, beating all zero-shot baselines, e.g. +9.3 SR over SpatialGPT on R2R (48.4) and +21.6 SR over VLN-Zero on R2R-CE (42.4). It matches supervised agents such as VLN-BERT and PREVALENT on R2R and DUET on REVERIE, and approaches ETPNav/HNR on R2R-CE. It remains below ScaleVLN and Efficient-VLN.
limitations: Requires pre-exploration and an available 3D point cloud (assumed from Matterport3D, SLAM robustness not evaluated), which deviates from standard online VLN and adds computation overhead.
Room segmentation is unreliable in open spaces and needed manual correction for large regions; annotation quality strongly affects results (GT variant is better).
Continuous-environment evaluation uses small random subsets (100/200 episodes); integrating SSG into supervised agents is unexplored, and Qwen3-VL-Plus did not benefit.
